Zoe Park: Quick follow-up to the allocator RFC -> prototype notes. Wanted to capture an adaptive bounded compact runner that uses an indirection header and a short retire window. Short thread.
Laura Chen: Love the direction. Can you sketch the adaptive part?
Zoe Park: Sure. Runner runs every epoch_ms (default 50ms). Each epoch it has two hard caps: time_budget_ms and pages_budget. It also maintains a rolling p95 measurement of token latency; if p95 > target, runner halves both budgets for the next N epochs. If p95 stays good, it slowly grows back.
Rohan Singh: How do we keep it from thrashing hot pages when budgets increase again?
Zoe Park: We combine the budget controller with a sampled hotness signal (1% access sampling -> tiny EMA). Runner filters candidates with hotness > hot_threshold. Also allocation descriptors can set defrag_priority (low|normal|high) which runner reads off metadata, not hot path.
Ken Matsui: Indirection header details? any atomic rules we should know?
Zoe Park: Header is two words: (addr_ptr, seq_counter). Migration sets seq to odd -> publish new addr_ptr -> seq++ to even. Readers do read-before/read-after check on (addr,seq) and retry if mismatch or odd. Pseudocode in-line: 
```nread_header:
  (p1,s1)=atomic_read(header)
  data=load(p1)
  (p2,s2)=atomic_read(header)
  if p1==p2 && s1==s2 && s1%2==0: return data
  else pause and retry
```
Zoe Park: That avoids global quiesce and keeps readers lock-free. Rare retries only when migrating.
Laura Chen: What about late DMA completions stomping a newly-reused page? retire window?
Zoe Park: On migrate, mark old page state=RETIRED with retire_epoch=current_epoch+retire_hold (default 1). Runner only hands pages back to allocator after retire_epoch. We also cap retired_resident_ratio (default 0.15) to avoid runaway memory during heavy defrag.
Rohan Singh: Memory pressure path? We can't keep retired pages forever.
Zoe Park: Forced reclaim: if memory_pressure or retired_ratio > max, runner can fast-reclaim retired pages but must zero them and perform an atomic fence before returning to allocator. Metric reclaimed_under_pressure_count increments.
Ken Matsui: Cost model for moving pages across pools/nodes? we need something cheap.
Zoe Park: Keep it linear: cost_move = bytes/est_bandwidth + pcie_latency + cpu_copy_units. Benefit = sampled_faults * avg_fault_cost. Move iff benefit*profit_factor > cost_move. We calibrate est_bandwidth and avg_fault_cost with telemetry.
Laura Chen: Telemetry and rollout plan?
Zoe Park: Add metrics: compact_epoch_duration_ms, pages_migrated_per_epoch, retired_pages, retired_ratio, header_retry_rate, reclaimed_under_pressure_count, move_cost_estimate_hist. Rollout: 1) unit tests + sim. 2) lab canary with epoch_ms=50 pages_budget=128 retire_hold=1. 3) small prod canary on non-critical cluster, watch p99/p95 token latency and retired_ratio.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: scheduled canary "adaptive-compact-v1" for branch "adaptive-retire-probe" on lab-node-4 :eyes:
Rohan Singh: One more edge: allocator metadata growth if we add defrag_priority. Keep it compact and pack into existing allocation descriptor to avoid hot-path cost.
Ken Matsui: Also consider a cheap sampling hook in the kernel path to update hotness (1% RNG). Sara's sampling module could be reused.
Laura Chen: OK next steps: Zoe will open a WIP PR with a small prototype + perf harness. I'll help with rollback runbooks and the p95 detector. Anyone want to pair on the prototype?
Ken Matsui: I'll help with the atomic header tests.
Rohan Singh: I'll help tune the move profit_factor and telemetry labels.
Zoe Park: Thanks all. I'll post the PR and a tiny diagram. Goal: safe continuous defrag without global pauses and no late-DMA stomps. :thumbsup:
